In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the first 3 weeks following myocardial infarct, the ergometric parameters are not reliable enough to decide on pharmacological and/or exercise prescription.

the FST is a reproducible test for the evaluation of the exercise capacity in patients with recent myocardial infraction, and the most important ergometrical parameters are reproducible up to a certain degree, depending on the individual response to exercise and on the presence of arrhythmias.
the short-term reproducible parameters in FST after myocardial infraction are the total work performed (up to 100%) and the S-T segment depression (up to 90%) and elevation (up to 98%).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FST are reproducible up to +/- 1 SD of normal values for HR, SBP, TWP and VO 2.
the reproducibility of FST parameters is good for TWP and VO 2, but not for HR, SBP and arrhythmias, particularly when these values exceed the normal values by more then +/- 1 SD.

, when the HR and SBP do not exceed the mean values obtained in the control group by more than +/- SD, the ergometric parameters are highly reproducible and can be used as an index of the patient's clinical condition.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the short-term reproducible of FST parameters is good in patients with a recent myocardial infraction, but it depends on the presence of arrhythmias, S-T segment depression, HR and SBP values exceeding the mean values by more than +1 SD.
the reproducibility of most ergometric parameters is very good in patients who underwent a functional stress 35 days after a recent myocardial infraction.

the short-term reprocibility of the most impotant ergometric parameters is very good and that it is necessary to repeat the FST in patients with HR or SBP exceeding normal limits by more than +/- SD to obtain more reliable data for the prescription of pharmacological and exercise treatment.
